A boundary map, a prior transcript or an extracted JSON is **not** proof that the original binary is readable. The evidence class on every row below says exactly how far the verification actually went.

| class | meaning |
|---|---|
| DERIVED_RECORD_ONLY | A prior artifact describes the source. This is NOT binary readability. |
| CONNECTOR_IDENTIFIED | The connector returns the file's identity and byte size, but the binary has not been opened in this environment. |
| CONNECTOR_TEXT_READABLE | The connector returned the file's text. The binary is readable by the connector; byte-level properties are still unverified locally. |
| LOCAL_BINARY_HASH_VERIFIED | The binary is on local disk, its SHA-256 matches a pinned identity, and its internal structure has been opened and counted. |

## K5 — the binary that was believed unavailable

The PL06 harvest package recorded the module DOCX as held externally by identity and not present in this repository. ### Anchor probe — the boundary map checked against the binary

Each frozen paragraph index was opened in the document and its text read. This is what proves the boundary map; the boundary map does not prove itself.

| 4704 | K5-PL06-T03-B03 | start | 3.5 Infrastruktur | Infrastruktur | yes |
| 4815 | K5-PL06-T03-B04 | start | 3.6 Badan Air (Water Body) | Badan Air (Water Body) | yes |
| 4951 | K5-PL06-T03-B04 | end_before | 3.7 Pencahayaan / Lighting | Pencahayaan / Lighting | yes |
| 5220 | K5-PL06-T04-B01 | start | 4.0 PENJAAGAAN DAN PENYELENGGARAAN | PENJAAGAAN DAN PENYELENGGARAAN | yes |
| 5360 | K5-PL06-T05-B01 | start | 5.0 PENGURUSAN KUALITI PROJEK | PENGURUSAN KUALITI PROJEK | yes |
| 5543 | K5-PL06-T06-B01 | start | 6.0 PERLINDUNGAN DAN PENAMBAHBAIKAN ALAM SEKITAR | PERLINDUNGAN DAN PENAMBAHBAIKAN ALAM SEKITAR | yes |
| 5705 | K5-PL06-T06-B01 | end_before | 7.0 DEMOBILISASI | DEMOBILISASI | yes |

The frozen anchors carry a section numeral — '3.5 Infrastruktur' — that the paragraph text does not. Word supplies the numeral from list numbering, so the body text is just 'Infrastruktur'. The anchor match is therefore on heading TEXT, and this run says so rather than claiming the anchor string appears verbatim in the document.

## K3 and K2 — reached through the connector, not through disk

Both packages were located under the official source root `1JRa1p9oGjZTWz1L6-1NPH2cW3jJpUKRF`. The K5 folder is confirmed independently: the PL06 custody record already pins Drive folder 1p18qHATFfn0oLHyCvYOfA8rQQlxkwJXS and file 16j15Knt75d1ybg1i1E2SWfeUfMRmcbJ4 for the module DOCX, and that folder is child 5 here. K2 and K3 are read off the same numbering, and each is corroborated by its own contents: folder 2 holds a single construction-management monolith, folder 3 holds exactly nine PL01-PL09 PDFs. Both match the brief's description.

Byte sizes come from Drive metadata. **No SHA-256 was computed for any K3 or K2 file**, because computing one needs the binary on local disk and it is not there. The field says `SHA256_NOT_COMPUTED_NO_LOCAL_BINARY` rather than carrying a plausible-looking value.

One readability probe was run against K3 PL03:

```
outcome            = TEXT_RETURNED_IN_FULL
page markers       = 9  (last: Muka Surat: 9/9)
LATIHAN present    = true
SKEMA JAWAPAN      = true
```

One probe is enough to establish that the connector opens this package's PDFs and returns their text with page markers intact. It is NOT a substitute for byte-level verification, which needs the binary on local disk.

### K2 size caveat

At 25,043,306 bytes this is the largest single source in the project. The connector warns that text may be incomplete for very large files, so any structural reading of it is bounded by that and is recorded as bounded, not as complete.
